claims.statement: Code is grouped by domain (DDD-influenced layout, TES-68) into four layers: app/ thin routes, modules/<domain>/{data,domain,ui} one module per PRD FR (14 domains), shared/ leaf level, and lib/supabase/ as the external data boundary; new code goes inside its owning module, not new top-level folders.

No business logic lives in app/: Server Components fetch via a module's data/ layer and compose module UI over shared/ui primitives (review-level rule), as exemplified by the dashboard and billing pages importing data/, domain/, and ui/ surfaces of multiple modules.
The import direction app → modules → shared → lib/supabase is ESLint-enforced via import/no-restricted-paths zones in eslint.config.mjs covering the app/, modules/, shared/, and lib/ trees.

Another module's data/ is private to every other module: its public surface is domain/ + ui/, and only app/ may fetch from any module's data/; the lint zones are generated per domain from the 14-entry domains array in eslint.config.mjs.

shared/ is the leaf level and must never import modules/ or app/ (lint-enforced); it contains the single-file shared/types.ts UI domain types, props-only shared/ui/ primitives (a shared/ui component that reads data or encodes business rules moves to its owning module), shared/vocab.ts fixed TESDA vocabulary, and shared/text.ts copy helpers — shared/mocks/ was removed entirely in the mock-data retirement.

Only module data/ layers (besides lib/supabase itself) may import lib/supabase/database.types.ts; app/, shared/, and modules' ui/ and domain/ are lint-blocked from raw DB row types and must import domain types instead.

Two type families stay deliberately separate: the generated lib/supabase/database.types.ts (raw rows with Row/Insert/Update per table plus seven Postgres enums) and hand-written shared/types.ts (UI domain types, with Batch as a hub type referencing seven other shapes from the file's domain sections); the mappers in module data/ layers are the only seam between them.

Every entity contract follows fetch → map → derive per the reference implementation modules/batches/data/batches.ts: fetch is a typed Supabase query whose rows are scoped by RLS (never manually filtered by tenant in JS), map is a pure DB-row to domain translation, derive computes lifecycle/date helpers.

mapBatchRow is pure (no I/O), exported for unit tests, and marks schema gaps with TODO(contract) defaults so the UI shape stays valid — e.g. billingDeadline and daysToBilling stand in on end_date because no billing_deadline column exists yet.

Data functions return discriminated snapshots with a core trio: unconfigured when isSupabaseConfigured() is false (renders an honest empty state — no mock or fabricated fallback exists), sync-failed when Supabase is configured but the query errors or the client throws (must surface a sync-failed banner), and ok carrying the mapped rows plus dataAsOf = freshest updated_at.

Modules extend the snapshot trio with genuinely distinct states: tenancy's ProfileSnapshot adds not-found (user authenticated via Clerk but no profiles row yet — webhook racing or failed, 'no access yet' rather than an error), and import's LearnerImportSnapshot adds validation-failed (CSV structurally invalid, checked before any Supabase client is created).

Raw error strings never reach the UI: the snapshot traps the error server-side while the route renders fixed copy — the dashboard's SyncFailedView says 'Couldn't reach Supabase' with 'Try again in a moment.' and a Retry link, and any appended label is a data-as-of stamp, never the error — and selectBatchesForDisplay returns an empty list for any non-ok status so failed or unconfigured fetches can never display substitute data (RULES forbids leaking raw Supabase/SQL errors, table names, or internal IDs).

DB_TO_UI_STAGE in modules/batches/data/batches.ts is a total (non-Partial) enum-bridge map so a new DB enum variant fails compilation until its UI treatment is chosen: training/assessment/billing map to UI train/assess/bill, entre is UI-only with no DB column, completed/blocked map to null and are special-cased by deriveLifecycle (all stages done / no stage active), and normalizeStatus surfaces DB blocked as UI pending.

The total-map bridge convention repeats across data layers — STAGE_TO_UI (documents), ACTION_TO_TONE (activity), DB_TO_UI_ROLE (tenancy, DB role a strict subset of UI roles), ASSESSMENT_RESULT_TO_UI (learners) — while DOCUMENT_ICONS is deliberately a Partial map because document_key is per-program configured data, not a closed enum.

Because a module's data/ is private, batches.ts hand-duplicates documents.ts's mapper logic (MISSING_DOC, mapDocumentRow, the catalog backfill in mapDocumentsMap/mapDocumentRows), kept in sync by hand rather than imported; activity.ts's toRelativeWhen mirrors batches.ts's toDisplayDate with the same unparseable-date-to-empty-string convention.

Cross-module data needs are satisfied by pass-by-parameter or by importing the other module's public domain/: tenancy's getProfileSnapshot takes the caller's Clerk user id as a parameter because resolving it is auth/data's private job, batches/data/metrics.ts imports documents/domain/compliance, and billing/data/billing.ts resolves school context through resolveTenant(tenantId, tenants) — a parameter with a tenant-id self-fallback, since no live tenant list is exposed yet.

domain/ layers are pure business rules with no I/O (e.g. urgencyTier in modules/batches/domain/urgency.ts) and are unit-tested with fixed as-of dates; shared/ must not re-export module code — domain logic extracted from the mock facade (urgency, billing readiness, dashboard metrics) now lives in module domain/ layers.

The per-module split of shared/types.ts was deferred in TES-68 while shared/mocks/seed.ts constructed 11 of the domain types inside shared/ (which can never import modules/); the mock-data retirement removed that blocker, RULES §2.16 is resolved as no-longer-applicable, and the split is unblocked whenever someone wants to do it — shared/types.ts remains a single file for now.

lib/supabase/ is the external data boundary: server.ts builds an anon-key client and attaches the caller's Clerk session token via the accessToken callback, throwing (NO_CLERK_TOKEN_MESSAGE) when no token exists instead of silently querying as anon (which RLS would answer with zero rows and no error); service.ts holds the RLS-bypassing service-role client reserved for server-to-server webhook provisioning only.
No index barrels exist anywhere — deep imports are the convention (shared/README, CLAUDE.md); modules with no code yet hold a README naming their FR and planned contents.

The domains array in eslint.config.mjs (14 entries matching the modules/ directory exactly) is the single source that generates the per-module data/-privacy zones — adding a new module requires adding it there or that module's data/ is not made private to other modules.

Mappers are unit-tested in tests/unit/ against the real generated contract: batches.test.ts derives the module-private join-row fixture shape via Parameters<typeof mapBatchRow>[0] instead of duplicating it, and the tests/ directory sits outside the lint zones so test files may import database.types directly, even though app code may not; real-Supabase RLS/tenant-isolation integration tests are still outstanding.

After any migration, database.types.ts must be regenerated and then affected mappers and domain types updated; migrations are additive and supabase/migrations/20260528160300_create_tenant_scoped_schema.sql is the canonical schema + RLS migration.

The 'no row means missing' document backfill is a data-layer decision (batches.ts and documents.ts seed every catalog requirement with MISSING_DOC, then overlay submitted rows), and a key still absent after backfill means untracked — to be read via modules/documents/domain/compliance.ts, never by indexing the map directly.

modules/batches/data/metrics.ts deliberately takes the requirement catalog (criticalDocumentKeys) as a parameter instead of importing or hardcoding one, because no single flat catalog exists — the live program_document_requirements table is scoped per scholarship program, so hardcoding would make the metrics correct for only one program at a time.

derive-layer sentinels protect downstream math: daysUntil returns Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY for a missing or unparseable date (the 'no known deadline' sentinel that sorts last and never triggers urgency tiers, since NaN would silently corrupt sorting and urgency math), toDisplayDate returns '' for null/unparseable input, and the dashboard KPI grid (modules/batches/ui/dashboard/DashboardKpiGrid.tsx) refuses to print the Infinity sentinel as copy.

modules/batches/ui/const.tsx, example.js, index.html, and shared-types2.ts are stray learning/design-bundle artifacts, not module code: const.tsx is a pasted TypeScript annotation exercise whose only project import is ./shared-types2, example.js is a console.log demo, index.html is a bare script tag loading example.js, and nothing in the app imports any of the four — the real public surface of batches/ui/ is what modules/batches/README.md documents; they must not be imported or patterned after, and new code belongs in the owning module's data/domain/ui (RULES §2.12).

The mock-data retirement removed shared/mocks/ entirely — no seed dataset or unconfigured-fallback mock (MOCK_BATCHES, MOCK_ACTIVITY, etc.) exists anywhere in the app anymore, surviving only in historical file-header comments — and unconfigured and sync-failed snapshots both render an honest empty state instead (RULES §3.19 forbids substituting mock or fabricated data).

RULES §3.19 makes the guard-clause ordering a named invariant: a real sync failure yields zero rows, so a route that checks 'empty' before 'sync-failed' would silently swallow the banner — app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx returns its sync-failed view before the empty check, and app/(dashboard)/billing/page.tsx does the same before its 'No batches to bill yet' view.

modules/batches/data/metrics.ts's getDashboardMetrics is a derive-only (no I/O) data-layer contract that exists at that path per the TES-30 issue text, but the live dashboard route uses modules/batches/domain/metrics.ts's deriveDashboardMetrics instead — docs/LIVE_DATA_MIGRATION_PLAN.md still flags the data-layer copy as a duplicate to 'decide which survives'.

Stale references to the removed mock data survive in comments and docs and should not be trusted: shared/README.md still lists mocks/ as a content and the old TES-68 deferral rationale, batches.ts's toDisplayDate comment and shared/types.ts's header cite the removed lib/data/seed.ts, learners.ts's seq comment cites the removed shared/mocks/seed.ts, and lib/supabase/server.ts's isSupabaseConfigured comment still says 'silent mock fallback' — RULES.md and CLAUDE.md, which record the retirement, win over these leftovers.
